The '''Hate Crime Statistics Act''', [https://www.fbi.gov/about-us/cjis/ucr/hate-crime/2010/resources/hate-crime-2010-hate-crime-statistics-act 28 U.S.C. § 534] (HCSA), passed in 1990 and modified in 2009 by the [[Matthew Shepard and James Byrd, Jr. Hate Crimes Prevention Act]],<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.fbi.gov/about-us/cjis/ucr/hate-crime/2010/resources/hate-crime-2010-hate-crime-statistics-act|title=FBI — Hate Crime Statistics Act|work=FBI}}</ref> requires the [[United States Attorney General|Attorney General]] to collect data on crimes committed because of the victim's race, religion, disability, sexual orientation, or ethnicity.  The bill was signed into law by [[George H. W. Bush]], and was the first federal statute to "recognize and name gay, lesbian and bisexual people."<ref>[http://www.thetaskforce.org/issues/hate_crimes_main_page/timeline Hate Crimes Protections Timeline] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140401073246/http://www.thetaskforce.org/issues/hate_crimes_main_page/timeline |date=2014-04-01 }}, [[National Gay and Lesbian Task Force]].  Retrieved on 05-04-2007.</ref> Since 1992, the [[United States Department of Justice|Department of Justice]] through one of its agencies, the [[FBI]], has jointly published an annual report on hate crime statistics.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www2.fbi.gov/ucr/hc2004/openpage.htm |title=Hate Crime Statistics, 2004 |website=Federal Bureau of Investigation |publisher=U.S. Department of Justice}}
</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.fbi.gov/news/stories/2014/december/latest-hate-crime-statistics-report-released/|title=FBI — Latest Hate Crime Statistics Report Released|work=FBI}}</ref>

On November 16, 2020, the FBI released its 2019 Hate Crime Statistics Act (HCSA) report with the total number of reported hate crime incidents rising 2.7% to 7,317 (2019) from 7,120 (2018).<ref>{{Cite web|title=About Hate Crime Statistics|url=https://ucr.fbi.gov/hate-crime/2019/resource-pages/about-hate-crime|access-date=2020-11-16|website=FBI|language=en-us}}</ref>
